_expect.name: Turtle Rock Area/ Small Stage Boulder

al_turtle_rock_area_small_stage_boulder.blurb: Small Stage Boulder is a compact stop within the Turtle Rock section of Horse Pens 40, the bouldering park near Steele. The Turtle Rock section lies close to the tin-roof shelter beside the trail. This one block holds six problems, all on the easier-to-middle side: two at V2, one V3, two V4 and a single V5. It suits a climber warming up or working through the moderate grades rather than chasing hard test pieces. Bring a crash pad, as with any boulder.

al_pillar_of_fire.blurb: Pillar of Fire is a single tall boulder in the Middle Bishop cluster of Bishop Mountain, the bouldering zone close to Huntsville. It sits a short way up the slope from the Baby Fin boulder. Six problems share the block, and most are modest, with a handful around V3 plus one at V2, then a couple of much harder lines reaching V6 and V8. The rock is rough and textured, yet the problems are still worth the visit. Plan on a walk of roughly fifteen minutes from the gravel lot to reach the main cluster of boulders around it.

al_proceed_boulders.blurb: The Proceed Boulders form a small row of problems in the Middle Bishop cluster at Bishop Mountain, near Huntsville. To find them, follow the cliff line south past The Point boulders. There are five problems here, mostly in the easier-to-middle range: a pair at V2, one V3, one V4 and a single harder line at V6. Middle Bishop as a whole holds the bulk of the mountain's established problems, so this spot works as one stop in a longer session, with the main cluster reached by a trail of about fifteen minutes from the parking lot.

al_guntersville_roof.blurb: Guntersville Roof is a large overhanging boulder beside the Bevil Trail inside Lake Guntersville State Park, reached from Highway 227. It is the standout formation among the scattered rocks of the Lake Guntersville area. Five problems start around V3 and climb steadily through V4, V5 and V6 up to V7, so the grades step up one at a time rather than clustering. A short scramble uphill from the road pull-off brings you to it. Bring a crash pad, as with any boulder.
